The model performs a systematic CNF‐style (CYK‐like) parse: it lists productions, tries every possible top‐level split of S→NT6 NT34, recursively checks each subspan against the exact grammar rules, even builds a bottom‐up table. No guesswork or approximate heuristic is used, nor is any code generated. This is a rule‐based derivation.  
Classification: rule-based

The model systematically applied the CNF rules, tried all possible splits of the 4‐token string under the S→NT6 NT34 production, expanded NT6 via NT33 NT19 (and further via NT31→t35, NT17→t66, NT19→t47), and NT34→t50, thus constructing a full valid derivation without guessing or using heuristics. This is a rule‐based approach. 

Classification: rule-based

The LLM’s response never builds a complete parse (e.g. a full CYK table) or enumerate every possible derivation, nor does it deliver a program; instead it informally appeals to which non‐terminals can produce which terminals and tries a few splits to “show” no derivation exists. That is heuristic reasoning, not a full rule‐based derivation or code. Classification: heuristic

The LLM never builds a complete, systematic derivation or CKY parse table to exhaustively show whether a derivation exists. Instead it informally maps terminals to possible nonterminals, tries a few splits against NT6’s productions, and rules them out by heuristic mismatches. This is not a full rule‐based proof of non‐membership, nor does it write executable code. It is using loose heuristic checks.  

Classification: heuristic

The LLM explicitly walks through the grammar’s productions, matches each nonterminal to the exact terminal in the string, and shows a full derivation from S to the target string. There’s no guesswork or heuristic appeal—just a strict application of the grammar rules. This is a rule-based strategy.  

Classification: rule-based

The LLM’s “analysis” consists of picking apart some productions in the grammar, noting that NT34 can only yield length‐1 strings and that NT6 has no recursion so can’t yield length‐13, and then concluding “no” without a full exhaustive derivation or counterproof. This is essentially guesswork based on superficial rule counts and lengths rather than a complete formal derivation.  Classification: heuristic

The LLM’s answer attempts to mimic the CYK parsing procedure—trying splits of the input string according to the grammar’s CNF productions and matching terminals to non‐terminals—but it never carries out a complete, systematic derivation or DP table fill. Instead, it uses partial checks and trial‐and‐error over splits without exhaustively constructing or ruling out every possible parse. There is no generated code or fully worked‐out derivation. This is best characterized as a heuristic strategy.  

Classification: heuristic

This is guesswork rather than a rigorous derivation. Therefore the strategy is best classified as:

heuristic

This is an informal, rule-matching guess rather than a complete, systematic derivation or code. Thus, it falls under:

Classification: heuristic

This is guess‐based reasoning rather than a complete rule‐by‐rule derivation or a coded algorithm.
